answers.answer: Each player puts their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that player's color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not playing and keep the player's own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “upright in their plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down card until cards are revealed; once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: “There is no individual turn order”; “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed”; “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is needed. The Target is the player receiving the most votes; with 3 votes against Red and 2 each against Blue and Green, Red alone is the Target.
answers.evidence: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”

answers.answer: Both tied players are Targets. Neither is protected by Ambush in this scenario, so both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to the successful Ambush exception.
answers.evidence: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated because Green did not vote for the Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.”

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count, producing a one-vote tie between Red and Yellow; both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds, so Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Pink survives because Pink voted for a tied Target, Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: Illustration: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink ... survives, leaving Red and Pink.”

answers.answer: No. The successful ambusher chooses only one player who voted for them, even if four players did so. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “cannot choose ... someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails.
answers.evidence: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. Since four survive, they continue with another conspiracy and vote, and only those surviving players participate in the subsequent vote.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: “That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars”; “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards, may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each “takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; each chooses one face down; “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; the players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated by it. Nobody collects the four central bars. Leave those four bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: No survivors: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.”

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The player choosing Share receives zero bars; the player choosing Steal receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The player choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the player choosing Steal receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Steal vs Grab One & Go: “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: The player choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the player choosing Share receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Grab One & Go: “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; Grab One & Go “gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: Each takes one central bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: “If both choose Grab One & Go, each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars are awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12, at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds “at least 25” and “at least 24”; “the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: The booklet requires tied leaders to conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. It does not end the tie after one extra Showdown if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in the round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total”; “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.”

answers.answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly, texting, or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; “speaking, whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, texting”; “the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.”

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID you want to target, and place it face down. If you suspect you are the Target and want to defend yourself, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: “To target someone, use the card matching that player's visible ID color”; “Each surviving player places one Voting card face down”; “play your Ambush card instead.”

answers.answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave survivors' IDs upright; those surviving players are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: After the round, if nobody has won, everyone returns. Keep any central bars left behind and refill the central pool to four bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.
answers.evidence: “Refill the central pool to four Gold Bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.”

answers.answer: No. Blue remains the only Target because Blue has the most votes; Blue's successful Ambush protects Blue but does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target, so they are eliminated under the voting requirement, unless individually protected by a successful Ambush.
answers.evidence: The summary does not describe this four-vote/three-vote example. It states: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target”; Ambush “does not ... prevent another player from being a tied Target”; and players who “did not vote for any Target” are eliminated.

answers.answer: The instruction is for tied leaders to conduct a Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. The summary says the booklet does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two tied players; its procedure and payoff table cover only two players, so the three-player arrangement is unspecified.
answers.evidence: “the booklet directs tied leaders to a Final Showdown”; “covers only two players. It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.”

answers.answer: Yes. In a double-Steal tie-break Showdown, players outside the tied pair each receive one bar from the deck. The tie rule considers the highest total anywhere at the table, so an outside player could become the winner if that bar gives them the single highest point total.
answers.evidence: Double Steal: “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; tied totals: repeat until “a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.”
